newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN STOCKS END DOWN ON OVERALL PROFIT-TAKING.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN STOCKS END DOWN ON OVERALL PROFIT-TAKING.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed lower on Tuesday on overall profit-taking amid weak confidence, but brokers expected a technical rebound on Wednesday.
The weighted index, which fell to as low as 9,759.36 points at one stage, closed at 9,807.74, a loss of 89.53 points or 0.90 percent, after bargain-hunting emerged to recover some loss ground.
Turnover was modest at T$141.9 billion.
"Weak confidence sent the index to test a 30-day-average at 9,737, which showed a strong support as buying then emerged," said United Securities analyst Lin Long-hsien.

Electronics, which plunged 5.21 percent on Monday, showed resistance to fall, sliding only 0.70 percent. Microchip giant Taiwan Semiconductor -- the market's top weighted share -- reversed its downtrend, ending up T$2 to T$153.
"Taiwan Semiconductor's comparatively strong performance helped stabilise electronics and the overall index," Lin said.
All major sectors fell, including financials, constructions, plastics and textiles.
Steel giant China Steel rose 30 cents to T$31.8 on sound outlook despite the government was auctioning 182 million state-owned shares of the firm, brokers said.
"This is a vote of confidence for China Steel as institutional investors have shown great interests in the company," said independent analyst Michael Hung.
Brokers said they expected a technical rebound on Wednesday, within a 9,750-10,000 range.
"The late buying showed that a strong technical rebound is very likely on Wedneaday," United's Lin said.
